nodes.source: I had been given the news by phone yesterday but essentially today was the final hurdle as far as my Cancer was concerned. Very nearly 6 months to the day from my diagnosis, which was on the 9th December 2004. This Cancer had been inside my body and spreading for quite sometime before that, there is no knowing exactly for how long either. With my symptoms and lead up in mind, possibly up to almost 2 years before I was diagnosed!!
nodes.text: Novico so mi včeraj povedali po telefonu, a v bistvu je bil današnji dan zadnja ovira, kar zadeva mojega raka. Skoraj natanko 6 mesecev od diagnoze, ki sem jo dobil 9. decembra 2004. Rak je bil v mojem telesu in se širil že kar nekaj časa pred tem, nihče pa ne more vedeti natanko, kako dolgo. Glede na simptome in dogajanje pred diagnozo morda celo skoraj 2 leti, preden so mi postavili diagnozo!!

nodes.source: I set off for the Hospital a little behind time today and even though it's a school holiday this week the traffic was horrendous. It seems that everyone visiting Clinic 8 today had suffered the same traffic fate as me, the place was empty.
nodes.text: Danes sem se v bolnišnico odpravil malo pozno in čeprav so ta teden šolske počitnice, je bil promet grozen. Očitno je vse, ki so danes prihajali v ambulanto 8, doletela ista prometna usoda kot mene, saj je bilo tam prazno.

nodes.source: Luckily I was seen to very swiftly and my bloods (Full Blood Count, U&E's & Tumour Markers) were taken almost immediately as I walked through the door.
nodes.text: Na srečo sem na vrsto prišel zelo hitro in kri (za celotno krvno sliko, U&E in tumorske označevalce) so mi vzeli skoraj takoj, ko sem stopil skozi vrata.

nodes.source: It wasn't long before I was seen to by my Consultant Dr. Savage.
nodes.text: Ni trajalo dolgo, preden me je sprejel moj specialist dr. Savage.

nodes.source: We went over my recent CT Scans and compared them to the previous ones taken almost 2 months earlier. A marked improvement was obvious and my lungs appear to be clearing up, although it's a slow process, it's exactly the progress that I could have hoped and wished for...
nodes.text: Pregledala sva moje nedavne CT-posnetke in jih primerjala s prejšnjimi, posnetimi skoraj 2 meseca prej. Očitno je bilo izrazito izboljšanje in videti je, da se moja pljuča čistijo. Čeprav gre počasi, je to natanko tak napredek, kot sem si ga lahko želel in nanj upal...

nodes.source: EXCELLENT !!
nodes.text: ODLIČNO!!

nodes.source: All that remains now are regular monthly blood tests, physical examinations and alternate chest X-Ray's which will become more and more spaced out as the years go by... yes years! I will be blood tested and checked up for the rest of my life, hopefully in about 5 years from now I will be given the 'ALL CLEAR' and then further blood tests will be taken annually for the rest of my life.
nodes.text: Zdaj ostanejo le še redni mesečni krvni testi, telesni pregledi in izmenična rentgenska slikanja prsnega koša, med katerimi bo z minevanjem let vse več časa... da, let! Kri mi bodo jemali in me pregledovali do konca življenja. Upam, da mi bodo čez približno 5 let rekli, da sem 'POVSEM ZDRAV', nato pa mi bodo do konca življenja enkrat na leto še naprej opravljali krvne teste.

nodes.source: I'm off the production line now and handed over to quality control!
nodes.text: Zdaj sem končal na proizvodni liniji in so me predali nadzoru kakovosti!

nodes.source: Amongst discussions about side effects that I have been suffering from, I reported a creaking sensation that I've recently noticed in my lower back, hips and legs. I haven't had any pain or discomfort, just this weird sensation like a creaking. My Doctor seemed to be a little worried about this and said it may be something of nothing, certainly not related to Cancer, more a side effect of chemotherapy and it would be best for me to go and have a Pelvis X-Ray immediately. The results of which would be discussed at the next patient meeting when the Doctors get together (most likely this coming Monday).
nodes.text: Med pogovorom o stranskih učinkih, ki me pestijo, sem omenil občutek škripanja, ki sem ga nedavno opazil v spodnjem delu hrbta, kolkih in nogah. Nimam bolečin ali neprijetnih občutkov, samo ta čudni občutek, kot da nekaj škripa. Moj zdravnik je bil zaradi tega videti malo zaskrbljen in je rekel, da morda ni nič posebnega, vsekakor ni povezano z rakom, prej gre za stranski učinek kemoterapije, in da bi bilo najbolje, če grem takoj na rentgensko slikanje medenice. O rezultatih bi se pogovorili na naslednjem sestanku o bolnikih, ko se zdravniki zberejo skupaj (najverjetneje ta ponedeljek).

nodes.source: I'm not too worried and hope the sensation will pass given time. Hold that thought!
nodes.text: Nisem preveč zaskrbljen in upam, da bo občutek sčasoma minil. Držimo se te misli!

nodes.source: Also whilst looking over my CT Scans my Doctor spotted some 'clips' that showed up. It did make me wonder but his mention of them was very cursory.
nodes.text: Med pregledovanjem mojih CT-posnetkov je zdravnik opazil tudi neke 'sponke', ki so bile vidne na njih. Res sem se zamislil, vendar jih je omenil samo mimogrede.

nodes.source: We said our good-byes and off I went for my Pelvis X-Ray. Again I was seen to very quickly and was X-Rayed within minutes of arriving at the reception. I asked very nicely if I could see the final images on screen, which the Radiographer kindly agreed to. Again there was mention of these 'clips' and that's not what the X-Ray was for!
nodes.text: Poslovila sva se in odpravil sem se na rentgensko slikanje medenice. Spet sem bil na vrsti zelo hitro in slikali so me že nekaj minut po prihodu na sprejem. Zelo prijazno sem vprašal, ali si lahko ogledam končne slike na zaslonu, in radiološki inženir mi je prijazno ustregel. Spet so bile omenjene te 'sponke', čeprav slikanje sploh ni bilo namenjeno njim!

nodes.source: Now it was getting me thinking, the Radiographer couldn't really shed any light on it for me so I set off to find out some more.
nodes.text: Zdaj mi to ni več dalo miru. Radiološki inženir mi ni znal zares pojasniti zadeve, zato sem se odpravil po dodatne informacije.

nodes.source: Essentially and at first I was quite mad/worried as nobody I asked seemed to know anything. There I was, left thinking that some foreign objects had been left in my body for no apparent reason and further surgery may be required to remove them, what do I know I'm not a surgical expert!
nodes.text: Sprva sem bil pravzaprav precej jezen oziroma zaskrbljen, saj se je zdelo, da nihče, ki sem ga vprašal, ne ve ničesar. Tako sem ostal z mislijo, da so v mojem telesu brez očitnega razloga pustili neke tujke in da bo morda potrebna še ena operacija, da jih odstranijo. Kaj pa jaz vem, saj nisem strokovnjak za kirurgijo!

nodes.source: At no point do I remember being told that metal 'clips' would be left inside me and now it has got me wondering how many of them there are, where they all are and exactly why are they there.
nodes.text: Ne spomnim se, da bi mi kadar koli povedali, da bodo v meni ostale kovinske 'sponke'. Zdaj pa se sprašujem, koliko jih je, kje vse so in zakaj natanko so tam.

nodes.source: I haven't really been given a detailed answer as yet but it seems common practise to have these clips left inside you after some surgical procedures. I would have loved to have been told this before hand, wouldn't you?
nodes.text: Podrobnega odgovora pravzaprav še nisem dobil, vendar se zdi, da je po nekaterih kirurških posegih običajno pustiti te sponke v telesu. Zelo bi bil vesel, če bi mi to povedali vnaprej, mar ne bi bili tudi vi?

nodes.source: Surgery is scary enough being out of your control. I think it would be nice to be put in the picture much more before you are cut open, especially when it is planned surgery!
nodes.text: Operacija je že tako dovolj strašljiva, ker nad njo nimaš nadzora. Mislim, da bi bilo lepo, če bi te precej bolje seznanili z vsem, preden te razrežejo, še posebej pri načrtovani operaciji!

nodes.source: Hmmm, not exactly sure what I am going to do about this but I need to find out more to put my mind at rest.
nodes.text: Hmm, nisem povsem prepričan, kaj bom storil glede tega, vendar moram izvedeti več, da bom lahko pomirjen.

nodes.source: That's all I can think of for now. I'll be back in a few days time to have a natter about the following...
nodes.text: To je za zdaj vse, česar se lahko spomnim. Čez nekaj dni bom spet tukaj, da malo poklepetam o naslednjem...

nodes.source: Note to watch TV... 21.00 on the 9th June 2005 on CH4 UK.
nodes.text: Opomnik za ogled televizije... 9. junija 2005 ob 21.00 na CH4 UK.

nodes.source: There is a documentary called "Bollocks to Cancer", I'll be very interested to see how close this documentary depicts itself to my individual experience.
nodes.text: Na sporedu je dokumentarec z naslovom 'Bollocks to Cancer'. Zelo me bo zanimalo, kako blizu mojim osebnim izkušnjam bo njegova upodobitev.

nodes.source: Apart from the above I am in good health and rapidly returning to full strength. I've been out and about filling my lungs with fresh air and eating well, watch out I could be knocking on your door soon for dinner!!
nodes.text: Razen zgoraj navedenega sem dobrega zdravja in se mi hitro vrača vsa moč. Hodim naokoli, polnim pljuča s svežim zrakom in dobro jem. Pazite se, lahko da bom kmalu potrkal na vaša vrata in prišel na večerjo!!

nodes.source: For those of you who are avid readers out there, you'll have made it this far with me and I thank you tremendously for that. Unless anything exciting happens now, entries will be very few and far between, although I do plan to keep the site well updated for the foreseeable future. There are new reference features coming to the site very soon and a few more pictures to boot.
nodes.text: Tisti, ki me zavzeto berete, ste prišli z mano vse do sem in za to se vam neizmerno zahvaljujem. Če se zdaj ne zgodi kaj vznemirljivega, bodo zapisi zelo redki, čeprav nameravam spletno mesto v dogledni prihodnosti redno posodabljati. Zelo kmalu bodo na njem nove informativne vsebine in za povrh še nekaj fotografij.

nodes.source: I am also going to be planning a party... aptly named "Tim's Ball" primarily for us all to celebrate the life we have been granted however difficult at times, please email if your interested in coming along! I haven't come up with a venue or any dates yet, I'm thinking August 2005 sometime to coincide with my birthday!
nodes.text: Načrtoval bom tudi zabavo... s primernim imenom 'Tim's Ball', predvsem zato, da vsi skupaj proslavimo življenje, ki nam je bilo dano, pa naj bo včasih še tako težko. Če bi radi prišli, mi pošljite e-pošto! Kraja in datumov še nisem izbral, razmišljam o enkrat v avgustu 2005, da bi sovpadalo z mojim rojstnim dnem!

nodes.source: 7th June 2005 - Tuesday
nodes.text: 7. junija 2005 - torek

nodes.source: Currently I'm attending a Cancer Support Group and my second meeting was this morning. Essentially we talk about our experiences with Cancer and how we and all around us have/are dealing with it.
nodes.text: Trenutno obiskujem podporno skupino za bolnike z rakom in danes dopoldne je bilo moje drugo srečanje. V bistvu govorimo o svojih izkušnjah z rakom ter o tem, kako smo se mi in vsi okoli nas z njim spopadali oziroma se še spopadamo.

nodes.source: Mostly what is discussed is pretty private stuff and individual to that sufferer, most of what I say is already here for you all to see! One of the subjects that was brought up today was the constant hurdles that face you during treatment, it's just one thing after another...
nodes.text: Večina tega, o čemer se pogovarjamo, je precej zasebna in značilna za posameznega bolnika. Večina tega, kar povem jaz, pa je že tukaj na ogled vsem vam! Ena od tem, ki smo jih odprli danes, so bile nenehne ovire, s katerimi se srečuješ med zdravljenjem, kar ena za drugo prihajajo...

nodes.source: Which brings me to some new information I have been given today. My recent Pelvis X-Ray results are in. All appears fine so far but my Doctors (whatever they are looking for) have been advised by the Radiologist that an MRI scan would be more suitable.
nodes.text: To me pripelje do novih informacij, ki sem jih dobil danes. Rezultati nedavnega rentgenskega slikanja medenice so prispeli. Za zdaj je vse videti v redu, vendar je radiolog mojim zdravnikom (kar koli že iščejo) svetoval, da bi bila magnetna resonanca primernejša.

nodes.source: I am now awaiting my appointment to come through the post, apparently it will be quite quick and I will have a follow up meeting to discuss the results.
nodes.text: Zdaj čakam, da po pošti dobim termin. Menda bo to kar hitro in potem bom imel še sestanek, na katerem se bomo pogovorili o rezultatih.

nodes.source: Now I'm a little nervous as to what this could be.
nodes.text: Zdaj sem malo živčen, kaj bi to lahko bilo.

nodes.source: Still no concrete information on the 'clips' that are inside me. I have had some very comforting emails from fellow patients who also have them so it's a little less worrying. Still I would like to know how many of them there are, where they all are and exactly why are they there! After all it sounds very much like they are there to stay and although I don't think I can notice them it would be nice to know exactly what I'm carrying about inside my body!
nodes.text: Še vedno nimam konkretnih informacij o 'sponkah' v mojem telesu. Dobil sem nekaj zelo pomirjujočih e-sporočil drugih bolnikov, ki jih imajo tudi sami, zato me zdaj malo manj skrbi. Še vedno pa bi rad vedel, koliko jih je, kje vse so in zakaj natanko so tam! Navsezadnje je slišati, da bodo tam tudi ostale, in čeprav se mi zdi, da jih ne čutim, bi bilo lepo vedeti, kaj natanko nosim v svojem telesu!

nodes.source: Ok I'm going to creak off in to life as best as I can make it, back on Thursday.
nodes.text: Prav, zdaj bom odškripal naprej v življenje in iz njega naredil največ, kar lahko. Vrnem se v četrtek.

nodes.source: 9th June 2005 - Thursday
nodes.text: 9. junija 2005 - četrtek

nodes.source: 23.30... Today is 6 months to the day since I was diagnosed with my Cancer, a disease that had spread throughout my body unbeknown to me apart from a niggling cough.
nodes.text: 23.30... Danes mineva natanko 6 mesecev, odkar so mi diagnosticirali raka, bolezen, ki se je nevede razširila po vsem mojem telesu, če odmislimo nadležen kašelj.

nodes.source: This time on the 9th of December 2004 I was lying in a medical assessment unit in West Middlesex Hospital, riddled with disease. My friends had gone home and I was left to wonder, alone in my room, what the future would hold for me.
nodes.text: Ob tej uri 9. decembra 2004 sem ležal na oddelku za medicinsko oceno v bolnišnici West Middlesex, prepreden z boleznijo. Prijatelji so odšli domov in ostal sem sam v sobi ter razmišljal, kaj mi prinaša prihodnost.

nodes.source: So, half a year later, I have been through 4 cycles of extensive BEP chemotherapy followed by major surgery and today I'm in remission from a Cancer that almost killed me. My story has been told and you've all been here to share it with me.
nodes.text: Torej sem pol leta pozneje prestal 4 cikle obsežne kemoterapije BEP, ki jim je sledila velika operacija, in danes sem v remisiji raka, ki me je skoraj ubil. Moja zgodba je bila povedana in vsi vi ste bili tukaj, da ste jo delili z menoj.

nodes.source: Strangely on this anniversary, a documentary was aired this evening called "Bollocks to Cancer". A documentary about a young Testicular Cancer sufferer and survivor. Although a different person and a short production to pack a lot of experience in to, it really brought back some vivid memories and experiences for me.
nodes.text: Po nenavadnem naključju so prav na to obletnico nocoj predvajali dokumentarec z naslovom 'Bollocks to Cancer'. Dokumentarec o mladem moškem, ki je zbolel za rakom mod in ga preživel. Čeprav gre za drugo osebo in kratko oddajo, v katero je bilo treba stlačiti veliko izkušenj, mi je obudila nekaj res živih spominov in doživetij.

nodes.source: It certainly did a good job of portraying what it's like to lie in hospital on BEP chemotherapy, the thought processes and feelings. My treatment was the exactly the same, I had an extra cycle. The wards were similar in layout although I did not have other Testicular Cancer sufferers around me. At the beginning, in one of my earlier male ward stays, all five of my fellow patients died. That was tough.
nodes.text: Vsekakor je dobro prikazal, kako je ležati v bolnišnici na kemoterapiji BEP, pa misli in občutke ob tem. Moje zdravljenje je bilo povsem enako, le en cikel več sem imel. Oddelki so bili podobno razporejeni, čeprav okoli mene ni bilo drugih bolnikov z rakom mod. Na začetku, med enim mojih prvih bivanj na moškem oddelku, je umrlo vseh pet mojih sobolnikov. To je bilo težko.

nodes.source: I have a different perspective on life now and have learnt a great lesson in mortality. A gift if you like, but not exactly the best way to receive it. It's difficult to describe the feeling, you have to experience it in one way or another for yourself, something which I do not wish on anyone.
nodes.text: Zdaj na življenje gledam drugače in sem dobil veliko lekcijo o umrljivosti. Lahko ji rečete darilo, vendar način, kako sem ga prejel, ni bil ravno najboljši. Občutek je težko opisati, na tak ali drugačen način ga moraš doživeti sam, česar pa ne privoščim nikomur.

nodes.source: My website lives on, as I do. I will be back soon with more information on further scans and tests that I am to have.
nodes.text: Moje spletno mesto živi naprej, tako kot jaz. Kmalu se vrnem z več informacijami o nadaljnjih slikanjih in preiskavah, ki me čakajo.

nodes.source: July 2005
nodes.text: julij 2005

nodes.source: Arrived at the hospital very much on time this morning, the traffic was a breeze.
nodes.text: Danes zjutraj sem v bolnišnico prispel povsem pravočasno, promet je tekel brez težav.

nodes.source: As instructed by phone earlier in the week I went straight to Clinic 8 for my X-Ray form and then to the MRI reception to register my attendance in good time for the MRI scan.
nodes.text: Kot so mi v začetku tedna naročili po telefonu, sem šel naravnost v ambulanto 8 po napotnico za rentgen, nato pa na sprejem za magnetno resonanco, da sem svoj prihod prijavil dovolj zgodaj pred preiskavo.

nodes.source: After registering at the MRI reception I went for my X-Ray. A very jolly bunch of nurses were operating the X-Ray machine today, I had a bit of a laugh and showed them my website. Although a serious condition I am monitoring with all of these X-Rays and tests, it's nice to have a bit of a laugh, normally at my expense... just to keep the spirits high, which is just as they should be!
nodes.text: Po prijavi na sprejemu za magnetno resonanco sem šel na rentgen. Danes je rentgenski aparat upravljala zelo vesela skupina sester. Malo smo se nasmejali in pokazal sem jim svoje spletno mesto. Čeprav z vsemi temi slikanji in testi spremljam resno bolezen, se je lepo malo nasmejati, navadno na svoj račun... da ohranjamo dobro voljo, kakršna tudi mora biti!

nodes.source: Straight after the X-Ray I went through for my MRI scan. My second MRI ever and I had the pleasure of putting a new scanner through its paces. I took a photo of the scanner (check the gallery soon), apparently it's worth 750,000 pounds sterling! I could certainly think of a few things to buy with that amount of money! However in this instance I think it's probably money well spent!
nodes.text: Takoj po rentgenu sem šel na magnetno resonanco. To je bila moja druga magnetna resonanca sploh in imel sem veselje preizkusiti nov aparat. Fotografiral sem ga (kmalu poglejte v galerijo), menda je vreden 750.000 britanskih funtov! Za toliko denarja bi si vsekakor znal zamisliti nekaj nakupov! Vendar mislim, da je v tem primeru denar verjetno dobro porabljen!

nodes.source: The X-Ray was to check up on my lungs and the MRI was a followup from my report to the Doctor that my hips/legs were giving off a creaking sensation which comes and goes at no particular time.
nodes.text: Rentgen je bil namenjen pregledu mojih pljuč, magnetna resonanca pa je sledila temu, ko sem zdravniku povedal, da v kolkih in nogah čutim škripanje, ki se pojavlja in izginja brez posebnega reda.

nodes.source: After my thorough zapping this morning it was off to Clinic 8 for my regular blood tests. This was quite quick and relatively painless (I am really getting used to these).
nodes.text: Po temeljitem jutranjem obsevanju sem se odpravil v ambulanto 8 na redne krvne teste. To je šlo kar hitro in razmeroma neboleče (res se jih že privajam).

nodes.source: Following a short wait I was seen by my Consultant, Dr. Savage. He had by that time had a chance to go over the scans from earlier today and was pleased to announce that they were all in order. Whatever they had suspected might be up with me as a serious Chemotherapy side effect was not the case and everything looked normal. I'll just have to put up with the creaking sensation and hope that it goes away sooner rather than later. Just as with the other side effects I have accepted and am dealing with on a daily basis.
nodes.text: Po kratkem čakanju me je sprejel moj specialist dr. Savage. Do takrat je že imel priložnost pregledati današnje posnetke in je z veseljem povedal, da so vsi v redu. Kar koli so že sumili, da bi lahko bil resen stranski učinek kemoterapije, se ni potrdilo in vse je bilo videti normalno. Pač bom moral živeti z občutkom škripanja in upati, da čim prej izgine. Tako kot z drugimi stranskimi učinki, ki sem jih sprejel in se z njimi spopadam vsak dan.

nodes.source: The X-Ray was also as clear as expected, there is damage to my lungs which is more apparent on a CT scan, however nothing nasty shows and in time they will hopefully get a lot better. I cannot really say that I notice any difference but then I haven't put any great amount of pressure on them yet. Just a couple of mountain bike rides out along the river which I seem to cope with very well, perhaps even better than before... but back then I suppose I was riding with developing tumours in my lungs that I didn't even realise I had!
nodes.text: Tudi rentgenska slika je bila čista, kot je bilo pričakovano. Moja pljuča so poškodovana, kar je bolj očitno na CT-posnetku, vendar ni videti ničesar nevarnega in upam, da se bodo sčasoma še precej izboljšala. Ne morem ravno reči, da opažam kakšno razliko, vendar jih še nisem posebej obremenil. Samo nekaj voženj z gorskim kolesom ob reki, ki jih očitno zelo dobro prenesem, morda celo bolje kot prej... ampak takrat sem verjetno kolesaril s tumorji, ki so rasli v pljučih, pa sploh nisem vedel, da jih imam!

nodes.source: I then paid a quick visit to the various wards that I have been treated in over the past months. It's nice to see the people who have treated me and give them a healthy smile, it makes them happy to know that 'the person' or 'the number' they treated is well again as quite often the case is that they hardly ever get to see patients again whatever the outcome. It also gives me good vibes to see them so happy that I am better and looking so much more healthy again.
nodes.text: Nato sem na kratko obiskal različne oddelke, kjer so me zdravili v zadnjih mesecih. Lepo je videti ljudi, ki so me zdravili, in jim nameniti zdrav nasmeh. Veseli so, ko vedo, da je 'oseba' ali 'številka', ki so jo zdravili, spet zdrava, saj se pogosto zgodi, da bolnikov skoraj nikoli več ne vidijo, ne glede na izid. Tudi sam se dobro počutim, ko vidim, kako veseli so, da sem bolje in da sem spet videti toliko bolj zdrav.

nodes.source: All in all quite a busy day at the hospital today. A small error in my blood test schedules has been rectified and I am now on a fortnightly regime as you will see from my updated schedule. Soon it will switch to monthly.
nodes.text: Skratka, danes kar pester dan v bolnišnici. Manjšo napako v razporedu mojih krvnih testov so odpravili in zdaj jih imam na dva tedna, kot boste videli v posodobljenem urniku. Kmalu bodo postali mesečni.

nodes.source: Unless anything exciting happens, I'll be back again on the 12th to report on my findings with the surgeon's team.
nodes.text: Če se ne zgodi kaj razburljivega, se spet vrnem 12., da poročam, kaj bom izvedel pri kirurgovi ekipi.

nodes.source: In the meantime I'll be making some changes and updates to the site so watch this space.
nodes.text: Medtem bom na spletnem mestu naredil nekaj sprememb in posodobitev, zato spremljajte to stran.

nodes.source: 12th July 2005 - Tuesday
nodes.text: 12. julija 2005 - torek

nodes.source: I came in to the hospital today for a pre arranged meeting with one of the Surgeon's team. Something that I had arranged for once, to clear up some outstanding queries.
nodes.text: Danes sem prišel v bolnišnico na vnaprej dogovorjen sestanek z enim od članov kirurgove ekipe. Za spremembo sem ga uredil sam, da bi razjasnil nekaj še odprtih vprašanj.

nodes.source: The scars are healing well although it'll be sometime indeed before they fade from the red lines that currently show. I have some numbness around and below my groin scar site (the Orchiectomy scar), this is totally normal and to be expected.
nodes.text: Brazgotine se lepo celijo, čeprav bo trajalo še kar nekaj časa, preden zdaj vidne rdeče črte zbledijo. Okoli in pod brazgotino v dimljah (brazgotino po orhiektomiji) imam nekoliko omrtvičen predel, kar je povsem normalno in pričakovano.

nodes.source: The clips... well this is something that I feel has still not been put to bed properly. For one thing I was told I cannot physically have one (just so I can show you all and for a reference as to what I have inside me). The other and more important factor is that there are no notes on exactly how many of these clips were used or their locations within my body.
nodes.text: Sponke... no, glede tega imam občutek, da zadeva še vedno ni ustrezno zaključena. Najprej so mi povedali, da mi ene ne morejo dati (samo zato, da bi jo lahko pokazal vsem vam in za predstavo o tem, kaj imam v sebi). Druga in pomembnejša stvar pa je, da ni zapiskov o tem, koliko natanko teh sponk so uporabili in kje v mojem telesu so.

nodes.source: In fact and according to the doctor I saw today, there are no notes on my surgery or the procedure whatsoever, I find this odd.
nodes.text: Pravzaprav po besedah zdravnika, s katerim sem govoril danes, sploh ni nobenih zapiskov o moji operaciji ali posegu, kar se mi zdi čudno.

nodes.source: I did manage to find out that the clips are made of a type of plastic called Silastic with titanium hinges, but even then the doctor was vague about this.
nodes.text: Uspelo mi je izvedeti, da so sponke izdelane iz vrste plastike, imenovane Silastic, s titanovimi tečaji, a tudi glede tega je bil zdravnik precej nedoločen.

nodes.source: 15th July 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 15. julija 2005 - petek

nodes.source: My first blood test in another hospital.
nodes.text: Moj prvi krvni test v drugi bolnišnici.

nodes.source: I had a meeting today at the Mulberry Centre so I thought it best to get my routine blood test carried out at West Middlesex Hospital as it is right next door and very local to where I live!
nodes.text: Danes sem imel sestanek v centru Mulberry, zato se mi je zdelo najbolje rutinski krvni test opraviti v bolnišnici West Middlesex, saj je tik zraven in zelo blizu mojega doma!

nodes.source: An all new environment to me so I asked at main reception where the outpatients blood test department was. I was swiftly and accurately directed.
nodes.text: Zame povsem novo okolje, zato sem na glavnem sprejemu vprašal, kje je oddelek za ambulantni odvzem krvi. Hitro in natančno so mi pokazali pot.

nodes.source: Most of West Middlesex Hospital is now relatively new buildings and the blood test department appeared clean and new. The nurses were chatty, they were so quiet I had to knock on the door and butt in on their gossip in order to get my blood test done.
nodes.text: Večina bolnišnice West Middlesex je zdaj v razmeroma novih stavbah in oddelek za odvzem krvi je bil videti čist in nov. Sestre so bile zgovorne. Bilo je tako malo dela, da sem moral potrkati na vrata in prekiniti njihov klepet, da so mi vzeli kri.

nodes.source: All in all a nice experience in what was a foreign environment for me. I'll be coming back for more blood tests here in the future!
nodes.text: Skratka, prijetna izkušnja v okolju, ki mi je bilo tuje. V prihodnje bom še prihajal sem na krvne teste!

nodes.source: August 2005
nodes.text: avgust 2005

nodes.source: 5th August 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 5. avgusta 2005 - petek

nodes.source: Routine blood test and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danes v bolnišnici Charing Cross rutinski krvni test in sestanek z mojim specialistom.

nodes.source: Everything looking good so far, my markers remain at normal and full blood count results now fall within the normal values although still at the bottom end of the spectrum.
nodes.text: Za zdaj je vse videti dobro. Moji označevalci ostajajo normalni in tudi rezultati celotne krvne slike zdaj sodijo med normalne vrednosti, čeprav so še vedno na spodnjem koncu razpona.

nodes.source: Physical examination carried out, all good.
nodes.text: Opravljen telesni pregled, vse v redu.

nodes.source: After the meeting I was sent for an additional blood test to check my testosterone levels, this is a new one for me. I told the Phlebotomist to be careful with the tube of blood he took as it may blow the testing machine up if they are not careful. I haven't noticed any of the low testosterone symptoms as yet, if anything I'm worse than before!
nodes.text: Po sestanku so me poslali na dodaten krvni test za preverjanje ravni testosterona, to je zame nekaj novega. Osebi, ki mi je vzela kri, sem rekel, naj bo z epruveto previdna, saj bi lahko razneslo aparat za analizo, če ne bodo pazili. Doslej nisem opazil nobenih simptomov nizkega testosterona, če že kaj, sem hujši kot prej!

nodes.source: Have you noticed I don't mention the endless needle worries anymore, I have mentally got used to them and the sites used for taking blood from me have become immune to needle pricks. Either that or I haven't had a bad experience recently!!
nodes.text: Ste opazili, da ne omenjam več neskončnih skrbi zaradi igel? V glavi sem se jih že navadil in mesta, kjer mi jemljejo kri, so postala imuna na vbode. Ali pa samo zadnje čase nisem imel slabe izkušnje!!

nodes.source: 9th August 2005 - Tuesday
nodes.text: 9. avgusta 2005 - torek

nodes.source: 8 months since initial diagnosis today. It passed without me thinking of it at all, I rarely think of the diagnosis anniversaries anymore.
nodes.text: Danes je 8 mesecev od prvotne diagnoze. Dan je minil, ne da bi sploh pomislil na to, saj o obletnicah diagnoze le še redko razmišljam.

nodes.source: Talking of anniversaries I'm going to make it to another birthday very soon, on the 22nd August 2005 I will be another year older. In the past -like many of you out there I'm sure- I didn't like to think of getting another year older, but now at each birthday I'll be grateful I've been given the opportunity to live another year! Let's face it, luckily I'm a survivor and hopefully many, many more birthdays will now pass me by!
nodes.text: Ko že govorim o obletnicah, zelo kmalu bom dočakal še en rojstni dan. 22. avgusta 2005 bom še eno leto starejši. Včasih - prepričan sem, da tako kot mnogi med vami - nisem rad razmišljal o tem, da bom še eno leto starejši, zdaj pa bom ob vsakem rojstnem dnevu hvaležen, da sem dobil priložnost živeti še eno leto! Priznajmo, na srečo sem preživel in upam, da bom zdaj dočakal še mnogo, mnogo rojstnih dni!

nodes.source: Strangely, on this day today, fell a talk on Testicular Cancer at an Army base not too far from where I live. Given by the inimitable checkemlads.com crew, Mick Riley and Phil Morris (new pictures in my gallery) to a large audience of first year recruits, a perfect target audience. I was introduced and applauded for all that I had been through, something I'm sure no soldier however 'hard' would like to confront.
nodes.text: Po nenavadnem naključju je bilo prav danes v vojašnici nedaleč od mojega doma predavanje o raku mod. Pred veliko skupino nabornikov prvega letnika, idealnim ciljnim občinstvom, sta ga vodila neponovljiva člana ekipe checkemlads.com Mick Riley in Phil Morris (nove fotografije v moji galeriji). Predstavili so me in zaploskali za vse, kar sem prestal, za nekaj, s čimer se, prepričan sem, ne bi rad spoprijel noben vojak, pa naj bo še tako 'trd'.

nodes.source: I've also committed myself to a tandem sky dive with an Army team, on the 2nd of September 2005 with Mick and hopefully Phil. Jumping out of a plane at 13,000 feet was not something I had in mind to do in my life, but now I jump at every opportunity given to me (pardon the pun).
nodes.text: Obljubil sem tudi, da bom 2. septembra 2005 z Mickom in upam tudi s Philom skočil s padalom v tandemu z vojaško ekipo. Skok iz letala na višini 13.000 čevljev ni bil nekaj, kar bi si v življenju nameraval privoščiti, zdaj pa zagrabim oziroma skočim v vsako ponujeno priložnost (oprostite besedni igri).

nodes.source: 12th August 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 12. avgusta 2005 - petek

nodes.source: Blood test day today, popped in to my local hospital for it. Again the department was a ghost town, I caught the nurse in charge and was soon given my test.
nodes.text: Danes je dan krvnega testa, zato sem skočil v krajevno bolnišnico. Oddelek je bil spet kot mesto duhov. Ujel sem odgovorno sestro in kmalu so mi opravili test.

nodes.source: Each time I go along to these tests at another hospital I have a special letter and dispatch sticker to hand over. This makes sure that my blood tubes reach the right place.
nodes.text: Vsakič, ko grem na te teste v drugo bolnišnico, jim izročim posebno pismo in nalepko za pošiljanje. To zagotovi, da moje epruvete s krvjo pridejo na pravo mesto.

nodes.source: Only 10 days to go and I'll make it to being another year older!
nodes.text: Še samo 10 dni in bom dočakal še eno leto več!

nodes.source: 26th August 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 26. avgusta 2005 - petek

nodes.source: Blood test day today, popped in to my local hospital for it. This time the department was full with people. I had to wait an hour before I was seen and tested, even then the nurse (a REED temp) did not know what to do with my paperwork, I had to explain how to take my blood, how much to take and what to do with the letter and sticker that I had brought for him.
nodes.text: Danes je dan krvnega testa, zato sem skočil v krajevno bolnišnico. Tokrat je bil oddelek poln ljudi. Preden sem prišel na vrsto in so mi vzeli kri, sem moral čakati eno uro, pa še takrat zdravstveni tehnik (začasni delavec agencije REED) ni vedel, kaj storiti z mojo dokumentacijo. Moral sem mu razložiti, kako naj mi vzame kri, koliko je potrebuje ter kaj naj naredi s pismom in nalepko, ki sem mu ju prinesel.

nodes.source: Quite easily the worst experience of a blood test I have had to date, short of dragging me around the room whilst holding a needle which was stuck in my arm, the test was very uncomfortable indeed and it took 2 attempts at getting anything out of me. I was glad to get out of there! Still suffering with a few of those lasting Chemotherapy symptoms, which could possibly go on for a long time to come.
nodes.text: Zlahka najslabša izkušnja z odvzemom krvi doslej. Manjkalo je samo še to, da bi me z iglo, zabodeno v roko, vlekel po sobi; odvzem je bil res zelo neprijeten in šele v 2 poskusih je uspel kaj spraviti iz mene. Vesel sem bil, ko sem odšel! Še vedno me pesti nekaj tistih dolgotrajnih simptomov zaradi kemoterapije, ki bi lahko trajali še dolgo.

nodes.source: Here's an update...
nodes.text: Tu so najnovejše informacije...

nodes.source: Tiredness
nodes.text: Utrujenost

nodes.source: (occasional)
nodes.text: (občasno)

nodes.source: Peripheral Neuropathy
nodes.text: Periferna nevropatija

nodes.source: (less apparent)
nodes.text: (manj opazno)

nodes.source: Tinnitus
nodes.text: Tinitus

nodes.source: (apparent at all times, got used to it)
nodes.text: (ves čas opazno, navadil sem se)

nodes.source: Tiger stripes on skin
nodes.text: Tigraste proge na koži

nodes.source: (still apparent, should fade with time)
nodes.text: (še vedno opazno, sčasoma bi moralo zbledeti)

nodes.source: Lung twinges/pains
nodes.text: Zbadanje/bolečine v pljučih

nodes.source: (occasional) I have noticed that on the day after having had a few too many alcoholic beverages, the above symptoms are far more apparent. Think I'll go steady on the juice for a while!
nodes.text: (občasno) Opazil sem, da so dan po tem, ko spijem nekaj alkoholnih pijač preveč, zgornji simptomi veliko izrazitejši. Mislim, da bom s pijačo nekaj časa bolj previden!

nodes.source: My birthday passed relatively quietly, I had many well wishers and a few cards/presents to boot. All in all and in my case especially I suppose I kind of hoped for a big surprise on the auspicious day, making it another year alive was most certainly the celebration. Perhaps I'll have to pull my finger out and organise my 'Ball'. Still, I'm running hard away from a 6-8 month hole in my finances, which is catching up with me and hurting bad.
nodes.text: Moj rojstni dan je minil razmeroma mirno. Dobil sem veliko dobrih želja in za povrh še nekaj voščilnic ter daril. Glede na vse in še posebej v mojem primeru sem na ta slovesni dan menda nekako upal na veliko presenečenje, zagotovo pa je bilo praznovanje že to, da sem dočakal še eno leto življenja. Morda se bom moral spraviti k stvari in organizirati svoj 'Ball'. Še vedno pa skušam na vso moč ubežati 6-8-mesečni luknji v financah, ki me dohiteva in zelo boli.

nodes.source: Life afterwards
nodes.text: Življenje po zdravljenju

nodes.source: 14 February 2025
nodes.text: 14. februarja 2025

nodes.source: Looking back at Charing Cross Hospital
nodes.text: Pogled nazaj na bolnišnico Charing Cross

nodes.source: Charing Cross Hospital, 14 February 2025. My last visit before discharge from follow-up care.
nodes.text: Bolnišnica Charing Cross, 14. februar 2025. Moj zadnji obisk pred zaključkom kontrolnega spremljanja.

nodes.source: Some of you might remember this chapter of my life… 20 years ago, I walked out of this hospital after completing some gruelling chemotherapy treatment for Stage IIIb Testicular Cancer. I didn’t know what the future held or if I’d make it another 20 years - but I hoped.
nodes.text: Nekateri se morda spomnite tega poglavja mojega življenja ... Pred 20 leti sem odšel iz te bolnišnice po koncu naporne kemoterapije za rak mod v stadiju IIIb. Nisem vedel, kaj me čaka v prihodnosti ali ali bom dočakal še 20 let - vendar sem upal.

nodes.source: Recently, of all days, on Valentine’s Day, I walked out of those same doors for the last time. I paused, feeling a little emotional, looked back and took this picture.
nodes.text: Pred kratkim, prav na valentinovo, sem skozi ista vrata odšel zadnjič. Obstojal sem, malo ganjen, se ozrl nazaj in posnel to fotografijo.

nodes.source: Life is a gift, and sometimes the hardest journeys lead to the most meaningful milestones. Here’s to the next 20 years and whatever lies ahead! x
nodes.text: Življenje je dar in včasih najtežje poti vodijo do najpomembnejših mejnikov. Na naslednjih 20 let in na vse, kar nas še čaka! x

nodes.source: On 14 February 2025, I was discharged from the care of Charing Cross Hospital, twenty years after my original treatment. My HCG results continued to be below 2 (normal) at my annual February follow-ups.
nodes.text: 14. februarja 2025 so me odpustili iz oskrbe bolnišnice Charing Cross, dvajset let po mojem prvotnem zdravljenju. Na letnih februarskih kontrolah so rezultati HCG še naprej ostajali pod 2 (normalno).

nodes.source: See the HCG follow-up results
nodes.text: Oglejte si rezultate kontrolnih preiskav HCG

nodes.source: January 2015
nodes.text: januar 2015

nodes.source: Very nearly 10 years clear.
nodes.text: Skoraj 10 let brez raka.

nodes.source: So I'm about to reach the 10 year clear milestone, but with the saddest news.
nodes.text: Torej sem tik pred mejnikom 10 let brez raka, vendar z najbolj žalostno novico.

nodes.source: After my enduring experience with Cancer and brush with the edge of life itself, my precious and beautiful daughter, who is almost 4 years old, has just been diagnosed with a brain tumour. She's just about to undergo many years of chemotherapy, radiotherapy and proton beam therapy.
nodes.text: Po moji dolgotrajni izkušnji z rakom in bližnjem srečanju s samim robom življenja so moji dragoceni in čudoviti hčerki, ki je stara skoraj 4 leta, pravkar odkrili možganski tumor. Zdaj jo čakajo dolga leta kemoterapije, obsevanja in protonske terapije.

nodes.source: This is totally unrelated and in no way connected to my illness (genetically or otherwise), just complete and utter rotten luck. In fact I am finding it extremely hard to believe both mine and my partners luck, and of course that of my daughter. Who's child deserves such rotten luck? I have no words to describe how devastated we are. I can honestly say I would happily go through my illness all over again to take this away from my precious little girl.
nodes.text: To je povsem nepovezano in nima nobene zveze z mojo boleznijo (genetsko ali kako drugače), samo čista, neznosna smola. Pravzaprav izredno težko verjamem, kakšno smolo imava s partnerko, in seveda moja hči. Čigav otrok si zasluži takšno smolo? Nimam besed, s katerimi bi opisal, kako strta sva. Iskreno lahko rečem, da bi z veseljem še enkrat prestal svojo bolezen, če bi jo s tem lahko odvzel svoji dragoceni deklici.

nodes.source: You can follow her story from her website and on twitter at: www.eleanorstollery.com
nodes.text: Njeni zgodbi lahko sledite na njeni spletni strani in na Twitterju: www.eleanorstollery.com

nodes.source: Below in chronological order...
nodes.text: Spodaj v kronološkem vrstnem redu ...

nodes.source: September 2005 1st September 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: September 2005 1. september 2005 - petek

nodes.source: Routine blood tests, X-Ray and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danes v bolnišnici Charing Cross rutinske krvne preiskave, rentgen in srečanje z mojim specialistom.

nodes.source: Battled with the usual bad traffic in to London today, which meant I was slightly late for the meeting with my Consultant. Once I'd arrived and the blood tests were carried out, my Consultant had gone to an important meeting so I was seen by his Registrar instead.
nodes.text: Danes sem se na poti v London prebijal skozi običajen prometni kaos, zato sem malo zamudil na sestanek s specialistom. Ko sem prispel in opravil krvne preiskave, je specialist že odšel na pomemben sestanek, zato me je namesto njega pregledal njegov zdravnik specializant.

nodes.source: I was soon sent for an X-Ray and came back to the Registrar for the results. All good. After a brief chat and confirmation of my next check-up date I left the hospital.
nodes.text: Kmalu so me poslali na rentgen, nato pa sem se po izvide vrnil k specializantu. Vse v redu. Po kratkem pogovoru in potrditvi datuma naslednje kontrole sem zapustil bolnišnico.

nodes.source: 27th September 2005 - Tuesday
nodes.text: 27. septembra 2005 - torek

nodes.source: Blood test day today, popped in to my local hospital for it. Again the department was quite busy. I had to wait an hour before I was seen and tested.
nodes.text: Danes je bil dan za krvno preiskavo, zato sem skočil v bližnjo bolnišnico. Na oddelku je bila spet precejšnja gneča. Čakati sem moral eno uro, preden sem prišel na vrsto za odvzem.

nodes.source: My favourite vein isn't working too well anymore! It's gone a bit hard. Guess I'll have to find another good one which gives limited pain, whilst the other recovers!
nodes.text: Moja najljubša žila ne deluje več najbolje! Malo je otrdela. Očitno bom moral najti drugo dobro, pri kateri ne bo preveč bolelo, medtem ko si bo prejšnja opomogla!

nodes.source: The blood test only takes a maximum of 5 minutes and I was soon released with a couple of attempt holes covered by cotton wool and tape!
nodes.text: Odvzem krvi traja največ 5 minut in kmalu so me izpustili z nekaj luknjicami od poskusov, prekritimi z vato in lepilnim trakom!

nodes.source: I've got some more questions for my consultant to answer. Hopefully on my next visit to Charing Cross Hospital I'll get to see him. See you back here on the 7th October.
nodes.text: Za svojega specialista imam še nekaj vprašanj. Upam, da ga bom ob naslednjem obisku bolnišnice Charing Cross res videl. Spet se beremo tukaj 7. oktobra.

nodes.source: October 2005 7th October 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: Oktober 2005 7. oktober 2005 - petek

nodes.source: Routine blood tests and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danes v bolnišnici Charing Cross rutinske krvne preiskave in srečanje z mojim specialistom.

nodes.source: I had made a late appointment with my Consultant today as the plan was to go for a bite to eat with him after my routine check-up in order to discuss a web-site he would like me to look at developing.
nodes.text: Danes sem se pri specialistu naročil na pozen termin, saj sva nameravala po moji rutinski kontroli skupaj kaj pojesti in se pogovoriti o spletni strani, za katero bi rad, da razmislim o izdelavi.

nodes.source: During my 'check-up' conversations with my Consultant I always try to give a very good indication as to how I have been feeling since we last spoke and any symptoms that I might still have or have developed.
nodes.text: Med pogovori s specialistom ob 'kontrolah' se vedno trudim čim bolje opisati, kako sem se počutil od najinega zadnjega pogovora ter katere simptome še vedno imam oziroma so se na novo pojavili.

nodes.source: One symptom recently has been a few mild but odd headaches in the left side of my head, my Consultant didn't seem too concerned as my treatment has been very successful and consequent blood tests/scans have shown no signs of any new activity whatsoever, nonetheless he booked me in for a low priority MRI scan on my head!
nodes.text: Eden od nedavnih simptomov je nekaj blagih, a nenavadnih glavobolov na levi strani glave. Moj specialist ni bil videti preveč zaskrbljen, saj je bilo zdravljenje zelo uspešno, poznejše krvne preiskave in slikanja pa niso pokazali prav nobenih znakov nove aktivnosti. Kljub temu me je naročil na nenujni MRI glave!

nodes.source: My body has been through quite a battle over the past year, I would like to -try to- think that any or all of the pains I get from time to time, sometimes daily, are just part of recovery or even old age! As my Consultant once said to me, "each and every new pain I get from now on will come as a renewed and far more heightened worry to me". The likelihood of it being anything as sinister as before is pretty slim especially as time goes on.
nodes.text: Moje telo je v zadnjem letu prestalo kar hudo bitko. Rad bi poskušal verjeti, da so vse bolečine, ki jih čutim od časa do časa, včasih vsak dan, samo del okrevanja ali celo staranja! Kot mi je nekoč rekel specialist: "Vsaka nova bolečina od zdaj naprej bo zame pomenila novo in še precej večjo skrb." Verjetnost, da gre za kaj tako zloveščega kot prej, je precej majhna, še posebej s časom.

nodes.source: I have heard Cancer called the silent killer before, now I know what that really means. However, there are many positives I can turn to, one of which being that I am regularly checked up on at the hospital, so I must not ponder on what could be and just get on with my life, a plentiful one with a new perspective!
nodes.text: Že prej sem slišal, da raku pravijo tihi ubijalec, zdaj pa vem, kaj to zares pomeni. Vendar se lahko oprem na veliko dobrega, med drugim na to, da me v bolnišnici redno pregledujejo. Zato ne smem tuhtati, kaj bi lahko bilo, ampak moram preprosto živeti naprej, polno in z novim pogledom na svet!

nodes.source: Here's an update of symptoms...
nodes.text: Tukaj je posodobitev simptomov ...

nodes.source: Tiredness
nodes.text: Utrujenost

nodes.source: (more apparent)
nodes.text: (bolj opazno)

nodes.source: Peripheral Neuropathy
nodes.text: Periferna nevropatija

nodes.source: (less apparent)
nodes.text: (manj opazno)

nodes.source: Tinnitus
nodes.text: Tinitus

nodes.source: (apparent at all times, got used to it)
nodes.text: (ves čas opazno, navadil sem se)

nodes.source: Tiger stripes on skin
nodes.text: Tigraste proge na koži

nodes.source: (still apparent, fading)
nodes.text: (še vedno opazno, bledi)

nodes.source: Lung twinges/pains
nodes.text: Zbadanje/bolečine v pljučih

nodes.source: (occasional) Head aches/sudden mild pains (occasional)
nodes.text: (občasno) Glavoboli/nenadne blage bolečine (občasno)

nodes.source: I have to remind myself before going out for a few too many drinks that the day after brings on the above symptoms much more! No sympathy expected there!
nodes.text: Preden grem ven in spijem nekaj kozarcev preveč, se moram spomniti, da so naslednji dan zgornji simptomi precej izrazitejši! Tu ne pričakujem sočutja!

nodes.source: I managed to grab a business related chat with my Consultant following my check-up and hopefully will be working with him on a revised and informative web-site related to a very rare Cancer. I will of course post the link when it's launched!
nodes.text: Po pregledu mi je uspelo s specialistom na kratko poklepetati o poslu in upam, da bom z njim sodeloval pri prenovljenem in informativnem spletnem mestu o zelo redkem raku. Povezavo bom seveda objavil, ko bo zaživelo!

nodes.source: A few days back I went to lunch with my good friend and fellow survivor Milton Mermikides someone I'm sure you are familiar with if you have followed my story or are a recent reader of the entire story! We sat in a restaurant in a totally normal environment eating totally normal food, a surreal experience for us both after what we have been through. I hadn't seen Milton for sometime and he's looking really well as I think I am too (compared to what we both looked like in hospital anyway), in fact we hadn't known anything different of each other! Both Milton and I felt like shouting from the rooftops the elation we felt about being back in the normal world doing normal things and feeling normal again! Something which to external perception no one would have any idea of, we were just two blokes sitting in a restaurant eating!
nodes.text: Pred nekaj dnevi sem šel na kosilo z dobrim prijateljem in sotrpinom, ki je prav tako preživel raka, Miltonom Mermikidesom. Prepričan sem, da ga poznate, če ste spremljali mojo zgodbo ali pa ste jo nedavno v celoti prebrali! Sedela sva v restavraciji, v povsem običajnem okolju, in jedla povsem običajno hrano. Po vsem, kar sva prestala, je bila to za oba skoraj neresnična izkušnja. Miltona že nekaj časa nisem videl in res je videti dobro, kot mislim, da sem tudi jaz (v primerjavi s tem, kakšna sva bila v bolnišnici, vsekakor). Pravzaprav drug drugega drugačnega sploh še nisva poznala! Oba z Miltonom sva imela občutek, da bi z vrhov streh zakričala, kako vzhičena sva, da sva spet v običajnem svetu, počneva običajne stvari in se spet počutiva normalno! Od zunaj nihče ne bi imel pojma o tem, bila sva samo dva tipa, ki sedita v restavraciji in jesta!

nodes.source: November 2005 4th November 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: November 2005 4. november 2005 - petek

nodes.source: Routine blood tests, X-Ray and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danes v bolnišnici Charing Cross rutinske krvne preiskave, rentgen in srečanje z mojim specialistom.

nodes.source: Breezed in to Charing Cross, no traffic today.
nodes.text: Brez težav sem prispel v Charing Cross, danes ni bilo prometne gneče.

nodes.source: Saw my friendly Phlebotomists, I mentioned to them that they have now known me almost a year, as on the 10th December it will be 1 year since I was first at Charing Cross Hospital. Doesn't time fly when you're having fun!
nodes.text: Videl sem svoje prijazne ljudi za odvzem krvi in jim omenil, da me zdaj poznajo že skoraj eno leto, saj bo 10. decembra minilo 1 leto, odkar sem prvič prišel v bolnišnico Charing Cross. Kako čas beži, kadar se zabavaš!

nodes.source: I was soon seen by my Consultant. Not much to say today really, I collected some up to date printouts of blood results, had my physical examination and collected my X-Ray form. He wasn't happy with how the 'NHS system' had allocated a date for my MRI head scan, so this may now be prioritised a little higher and brought forward to as early as November or December 2005.
nodes.text: Kmalu me je sprejel moj specialist. Danes pravzaprav ni veliko povedati. Dobil sem nekaj svežih izpisov krvnih izvidov, opravil telesni pregled in prevzel napotnico za rentgen. Ni bil zadovoljen s tem, kako mi je 'sistem NHS' določil datum magnetne resonance glave, zato bo morda zdaj dobila nekoliko večjo prednost in bo prestavljena že na november ali december 2005.

nodes.source: Other than that he is very happy with my progress, the treatment has been very effective and I am well and truly on my way to making it back to 100%25 health - my blood results over the past few tests show that I am still just out of the normal ranges. It takes approximately 1 year for the effects of BEP Chemotherapy to fully dissipate from the human body, in some cases longer.
nodes.text: Sicer je z mojim napredkom zelo zadovoljen. Zdravljenje je bilo zelo učinkovito in res sem na dobri poti do vrnitve na 100% zdravje - moji krvni izvidi zadnjih nekaj testov kažejo, da so vrednosti še vedno tik zunaj normalnih razponov. Približno 1 leto traja, da učinki kemoterapije BEP povsem izginejo iz človeškega telesa, v nekaterih primerih tudi dlje.

nodes.source: Bumped in to a fellow patient in the waiting room, I met him along with his parents some time back during my treatment days in hospital and he is still battling hard it seems. I can only wish him and his family well in the face of Cancer which I am sure Charing Cross is doing everything it can to defeat.
nodes.text: V čakalnici sem naletel na sobolnika. Njega in njegove starše sem spoznal pred časom, ko sem se zdravil v bolnišnici, in očitno se še vedno trdo bori. Njemu in družini lahko samo zaželim vse dobro v boju z rakom, za katerega sem prepričan, da bolnišnica Charing Cross dela vse, kar je v njeni moči, da ga premaga.

nodes.source: Off for my X-Ray, as usual a quick and painless experience with what looked to my eye like a good result (the Radiographer kindly showed me the resulting scan), however it takes a few days for a Radiologist to check it out properly.
nodes.text: Nato na rentgen, kot običajno hitro in neboleče, z izvidom, ki je bil mojemu očesu videti dober (radiološki inženir mi je prijazno pokazal posnetek), vendar traja nekaj dni, da ga radiolog ustrezno pregleda.

nodes.source: Once again I was free to leave the hospital, back in to the open world and on with my life. See you again on the 2nd December 2005.
nodes.text: Spet sem lahko zapustil bolnišnico, se vrnil v svet in nadaljeval svoje življenje. Spet se vidimo 2. decembra 2005.

nodes.source: December 2005
nodes.text: december 2005

nodes.source: 2nd December 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 2. decembra 2005 - petek

nodes.source: Routine blood tests and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danes v bolnišnici Charing Cross rutinske krvne preiskave in srečanje z mojim specialistom.

nodes.source: Arrived behind time today, been rushed off my feet this week what with arriving back from abroad later than I expected.
nodes.text: Danes sem prišel prepozno. Ta teden sem bil strašno zaposlen, med drugim tudi zato, ker sem se iz tujine vrnil pozneje, kot sem pričakoval.

nodes.source: Blood tests carried out very quickly, I pretty much walked straight in and before I knew it I had given 4 test tubes of blood. One and most importantly for my tumour markers (HCG), two to monitor my general health (U&E's & FBC) and finally one for my testosterone levels.
nodes.text: Krvne teste so opravili zelo hitro. Skoraj naravnost sem vstopil in še preden sem se dobro zavedel, sem že dal 4 epruvete krvi. Eno, najpomembnejšo, za tumorske označevalce (HCG), dve za spremljanje splošnega zdravja (U&E in FBC) in zadnjo za raven testosterona.

nodes.source: Had to wait for my Consultant for a bit which was totally understandable as Clinic had all but closed for business and he had left to continue with his work elsewhere. Clinic reception kindly called him to see if he was free to come back for me.
nodes.text: Na specialista sem moral malo počakati, kar je bilo povsem razumljivo, saj se je ambulanta že skoraj zaprla, on pa je odšel nadaljevat delo drugam. Na sprejemu so ga prijazno poklicali in vprašali, ali se lahko vrne zame.

nodes.source: Everything still looking good as far as my recovery is concerned, testosterone levels are within UK normal ranges, last months X-Ray results have been studied and the -some would say, rather awkward- physical examination checked out all fine.
nodes.text: Kar zadeva moje okrevanje, je vse še vedno videti dobro. Raven testosterona je znotraj normalnih razponov za Združeno kraljestvo, rezultate prejšnjemesečnega rentgena so preučili in telesni pregled - ki bi se nekaterim zdel precej neroden - je pokazal, da je vse v redu.

nodes.source: Comments on last months X-Ray even stated that there is now little or no evidence of any damage in my lungs, something I am astounded by. A CT scan would most likely show up some scarring, but there is no need for a CT at this stage.
nodes.text: V komentarju k prejšnjemesečnemu rentgenu je celo pisalo, da je zdaj v pljučih zelo malo ali nič dokazov o poškodbah, kar me je osupnilo. CT bi najverjetneje pokazal nekaj brazgotin, vendar na tej stopnji ni potrebe po njem.

nodes.source: Certainly all signs of a fine recovery in progress.
nodes.text: Vsekakor sami znaki odličnega okrevanja.

nodes.source: My MRI scan has now been brought forward to the 19th December 2005 and my next routine check-up is scheduled slightly earlier on the 23rd December 2005, as I will be away when it is actually due around the beginning of the new year.
nodes.text: Mojo magnetno resonanco so zdaj prestavili na zgodnejši datum, 19. december 2005, naslednji rutinski pregled pa je predviden nekoliko prej, 23. decembra 2005, saj bom odsoten, ko bi moral biti dejansko na vrsti okoli začetka novega leta.

nodes.source: I'll put pen to paper (or keys to the web!) on my first diagnosis anniversary which is fast approaching on the 9th December 2005. I will not be celebrating as I don't think celebrating the diagnosis of a life threatening illness is very apt.
nodes.text: Pero bom spet vzel v roke (ali pa tipke priključil spletu!) ob prvi obletnici diagnoze, ki se hitro bliža, 9. decembra 2005. Praznoval ne bom, saj se mi praznovanje diagnoze smrtno nevarne bolezni ne zdi prav primerno.

nodes.source: 9th December 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 9. decembra 2005 - petek

nodes.source: The 9th of December 2005 passed relatively quietly for me and was certainly a day I choose to reflect on the year that has passed. Although it's been tough at times, I'm most certainly glad to still be here and to have out lived the "less than a year to live" statement.
nodes.text: 9. december 2005 je zame minil razmeroma mirno in ta dan sem vsekakor namenil razmišljanju o minulem letu. Čeprav je bilo včasih težko, sem zagotovo vesel, da sem še vedno tukaj in da sem preživel napoved 'manj kot leto življenja'.

nodes.source: This website has been a great help to me, as an outlet for my thoughts and fears during my treatment, surgery and ongoing recovery. It now stands as a testament, a message of strength and positivity to others. Others not only suffering with a similar illness or disease to mine, but for anybody who faces a challenge of such enormity in relation to life's twists and turns. You can win through, you have to just keep on going, keep looking forwards and stay positive. I did and look where it got me, still here and living life to the full.
nodes.text: To spletno mesto mi je bilo v veliko pomoč kot prostor, kamor sem lahko izlil misli in strahove med zdravljenjem, operacijo in nadaljnjim okrevanjem. Zdaj ostaja kot pričevanje, sporočilo moči in pozitivnosti drugim. Ne le tistim, ki trpijo za podobno boleznijo kot jaz, temveč vsakomur, ki se ob življenjskih preobratih sooča s tako velikanskim izzivom. Lahko zmagaš, samo naprej moraš, gledati v prihodnost in ostati pozitiven. Jaz sem in poglejte, kam me je to pripeljalo: še vedno sem tukaj in živim s polnimi pljuči.

nodes.source: Not many people remembered or reminded me of this day just a few close friends. I made a note of it in my diary, although I doubt I'll ever be able to forget what happened a year ago today, I have the scars to remind me forever.
nodes.text: Ni se veliko ljudi spomnilo na ta dan ali me nanj opomnilo, samo nekaj tesnih prijateljev. Zabeležil sem si ga v dnevnik, čeprav dvomim, da bom kadar koli lahko pozabil, kaj se je zgodilo na današnji dan pred enim letom. Brazgotine me bodo na to spominjale za vedno.

nodes.source: Has it changed me? Well, I have certainly been given the opportunity to see life with a different perspective completely, a gift if you like or simply a second chance in the face of death. At no point before in my life before this happened would I stop to think that a certain day would be the last day of its kind in my life, ONE LIFE, so as the 9th of December 2005 passes I will never see another day the same in my life. There is no ground hog day. So we only get one shot of this existence, make the most you possibly can of it.
nodes.text: Me je to spremenilo? No, vsekakor sem dobil priložnost pogledati na življenje s povsem drugega zornega kota, darilo, če želite, ali preprosto drugo priložnost ob soočenju s smrtjo. Preden se je to zgodilo, se nikoli v življenju nisem ustavil in pomislil, da je določen dan zadnji takšen dan v mojem življenju. ENO ŽIVLJENJE. Torej ko mine 9. december 2005, v življenju nikoli več ne bom videl enakega dne. Neskončnega ponavljanja istega dne ni. Za ta obstoj imamo torej samo eno priložnost, izkoristite jo, kolikor najbolj morete.

nodes.source: What are you going to do today and with the rest of your life?
nodes.text: Kaj boste počeli danes in s preostankom svojega življenja?

nodes.source: You never know what life has in store for you, what's around the next corner... this disease crept up through my body for over a year and a half, practically unbeknown to me, scary isn't it!
nodes.text: Nikoli ne veš, kaj ti pripravlja življenje, kaj te čaka za naslednjim vogalom... ta bolezen se je več kot leto in pol plazila po mojem telesu, skoraj ne da bi vedel zanjo. Strašljivo, kajne!

nodes.source: People ask me if I am 'cured' or 'recovered'. My understanding of being 'cured' of Cancer is there is NO cure, if you survive it and the treatment, you live in remission of the disease for the rest of your life, your body has shown the potential for Cancer so your chances are slightly higher than most (of it coming back), however there are many other health statistics that will beat this in to a minute possibility.
nodes.text: Ljudje me sprašujejo, ali sem 'ozdravljen' oziroma ali sem 'okreval'. Moje razumevanje 'ozdravitve' raka je, da zdravila NI. Če preživiš bolezen in zdravljenje, do konca življenja živiš v remisiji. Tvoje telo je pokazalo zmožnost razvoja raka, zato so tvoje možnosti nekoliko višje kot pri večini (da se vrne), vendar obstaja veliko drugih zdravstvenih statistik, ob katerih ta možnost postane neznatna.

nodes.source: Am I fully recovered? NO, I am still very tired; my body is recovering from the effects of chemotherapy, which will take sometime. Although to all external appearances I might appear fit and healthy, I just do not have the stamina or the tenacity I did before. It will come with time.
nodes.text: Sem popolnoma okreval? NE, še vedno sem zelo utrujen; moje telo okreva po učinkih kemoterapije, kar bo trajalo nekaj časa. Čeprav sem navzven morda videti v dobri kondiciji in zdrav, preprosto nimam takšne vzdržljivosti ali vztrajnosti kot prej. Sčasoma se bosta vrnili.

nodes.source: All this affects my work and my finances substantially enough to reverberate for a long time to come. There is no possible way you can imagine that you would have to plan financially for a major illness in your life, you just don't think it will happen to you.
nodes.text: Vse to dovolj močno vpliva na moje delo in finance, da bodo posledice odmevale še dolgo. Nikakor si ne moreš predstavljati, da bi se moral finančno pripraviti na hudo bolezen v življenju, preprosto ne misliš, da se bo zgodila tebi.

nodes.source: This Christmas should certainly be a better one; at least I'm not going to be eating a hospital Christmas dinner attached to a Chemotherapy IV drip!
nodes.text: Ta božič bi vsekakor moral biti boljši; vsaj bolnišnične božične večerje ne bom jedel, priključen na infuzijo kemoterapije!

nodes.source: I'm not sure how many of you out there still follow my story and have done so from its inception back in mid December 2004. It's been a long year for me, a life changing experience, how has yours passed?
nodes.text: Ne vem, koliko vas še vedno spremlja mojo zgodbo in ji sledi že od začetka sredi decembra 2004. Zame je bilo dolgo leto, izkušnja, ki mi je spremenila življenje. Kako je minilo vaše?

nodes.source: 19th December 2005 - Monday
nodes.text: 19. decembra 2005 - ponedeljek

nodes.source: Arrived early for my MRI appointment. The MRI department is normally a pretty busy place so I was kept waiting about 45 minutes for my scan.
nodes.text: Na magnetno resonanco sem prispel zgodaj. Oddelek za magnetno resonanco je navadno precej zaseden, zato sem moral na slikanje čakati približno 45 minut.

nodes.source: Usual procedure, remove all metals, credit cards and pretty much everything from my person apart from my clothes. You are given a little locker to store it all in.
nodes.text: Običajni postopek: s sebe odstraniti vse kovine, kreditne kartice in pravzaprav vse razen oblačil. Dobite majhno omarico, kamor vse to shranite.

nodes.source: Once in the scanner it takes about 30-45 minutes in total to complete an MRI brain scan, half way through there is an injection of a special colourant to further highlight areas of the brain.
nodes.text: Ko si v aparatu, celotna magnetna resonanca možganov traja približno 30-45 minut. Na polovici dobiš injekcijo posebnega kontrastnega sredstva, ki še bolj poudari področja možganov.

nodes.source: Whenever I go for these 'scans', be it X-Rays, CT's or MRI's I always try to judge the operators reaction once its complete, after all, I was fairly accurate in my judgement of the radiologists reaction to my first ever X-Ray over a year ago!
nodes.text: Vsakič, ko grem na ta 'slikanja', pa naj bodo rentgen, CT ali magnetna resonanca, skušam po koncu oceniti odziv izvajalca. Navsezadnje sem pred več kot enim letom precej pravilno ocenil radiologov odziv na moj prvi rentgenski posnetek sploh!

nodes.source: 23rd December 2005 - Friday
nodes.text: 23. decembra 2005 - petek

nodes.source: I was quite late for my appointment today and I paid for it (not intentionally I might add). Today's blood test was a painful one, the blood was taken from a not often used vein. The sister was chatting to me whilst the test was underway so my mind was taken off of the pain somewhat, still, I hate it when it hurts like that.
nodes.text: Danes sem na pregled precej zamudil in plačal za to (naj dodam, da ne namenoma). Današnji odvzem krvi je bolel, kri so mi vzeli iz žile, ki je ne uporabljajo pogosto. Glavna sestra je med odvzemom klepetala z menoj, kar mi je nekoliko odvrnilo misli od bolečine, vendar vseeno sovražim, ko tako boli.

nodes.source: My Consultant was called back from his staff Christmas lunch break which had almost begun (sorry!), just to speak with me. This was my last meeting with him before I was due to go abroad for a considerable length of time, a first since I had been ill.
nodes.text: Mojega specialista so poklicali nazaj z božičnega kosila za osebje, ki se je ravno začenjalo (oprostite!), samo da je govoril z menoj. To je bilo moje zadnje srečanje z njim pred odhodom v tujino za precej dolgo časa, prvič, odkar sem zbolel.

nodes.source: Everything checked out fine. Results from my previous tests were discussed. Nothing showed up on the MRI, bloods returning to normal values, all looking good so far. I am in the very high 90's in terms of percentage for making a complete return to normal health. I was given an X-Ray form as it was X-Ray time again and an appointment for almost immediately after I was due to return from my trip.
nodes.text: Vse je bilo v redu. Pogovorila sva se o rezultatih prejšnjih preiskav. Magnetna resonanca ni pokazala ničesar, krvne vrednosti se vračajo v normalo, za zdaj je vse videti dobro. Kar zadeva odstotek popolne vrnitve k normalnemu zdravju, sem visoko nad 90 odstotki. Dobil sem napotnico za rentgen, saj je bil spet čas zanj, in termin skoraj takoj po predvideni vrnitvi s potovanja.

nodes.source: Once at the X-Ray department I had quite a wait to be seen. I normally take most of the day out to do a hospital visit so this didn't concern me too much and after all my welfare is what is most important to me otherwise I would be no good to anyone. X-Ray done and I was free to go.
nodes.text: Na rentgenskem oddelku sem moral kar dolgo čakati, da sem prišel na vrsto. Za obisk bolnišnice si navadno vzamem večino dneva, zato me to ni preveč skrbelo. Navsezadnje je moje dobro počutje zame najpomembnejše, sicer ne bi bil nikomur v korist. Rentgen opravljen in lahko sem odšel.

nodes.source: January 2006
nodes.text: januar 2006

nodes.source: 27th January 2006 - Friday
nodes.text: 27. januarja 2006 - petek

nodes.source: Back from abroad. I was quite ill whilst away, towards the end of my trip, probably the illest I've been since treatment. It's a scary place to be when you're over 4000 miles away from your home comforts. I was glad to have been given the opportunity to get away for a well deserved break but at the same time I was glad to be back within my comfort zone.
nodes.text: Nazaj iz tujine. Proti koncu potovanja sem precej zbolel, verjetno najhuje od zdravljenja. Strašljivo je biti v takem stanju več kot 4000 milj od udobja doma. Vesel sem bil, da sem dobil priložnost oditi na zaslužen oddih, a hkrati sem bil vesel, da sem se vrnil v svoje znano in varno okolje.

nodes.source: Routine blood tests and meeting with my Consultant today at Charing Cross Hospital.
nodes.text: Danes v bolnišnici Charing Cross rutinske krvne preiskave in srečanje z mojim specialistom.

nodes.source: Good and relatively painless blood test (I like it when it goes smoothly). If you ever wondered what goes on at a blood test have a look at Milton's recent video here, this is something we have both become pretty much accustomed to over time!
nodes.text: Dober in razmeroma neboleč odvzem krvi (všeč mi je, kadar gre gladko). Če ste se kdaj spraševali, kaj se dogaja pri odvzemu krvi, si tukaj oglejte Miltonov nedavni video. To je nekaj, česar sva se oba sčasoma že precej navadila!

nodes.source: Was swiftly seen by my Consultant, again everything in order, physical examination out of the way and off I go!
nodes.text: Specialist me je hitro sprejel, spet je bilo vse v redu, telesni pregled opravljen in že grem!

nodes.source: My next appointment will be the last of my monthly check-ups, after which it goes to every 2 months with X-Rays on alternative visits as before.
nodes.text: Naslednji pregled bo zadnji od mojih mesečnih pregledov, nato bodo na vsaka 2 meseca, z rentgenom ob vsakem drugem obisku, tako kot doslej.

nodes.source: February 2006
nodes.text: februar 2006

nodes.source: 8th February 2006 - Wednesday
nodes.text: 8. februarja 2006 - sreda

nodes.source: A mental note... ONE YEAR CLEAR OF CANCER IN MY BLOOD!
nodes.text: Zabeležka v mislih... ENO LETO BREZ RAKA V MOJI KRVI!

nodes.source: Did anybody really notice, not a chance, "life goes on", something to always remember!
nodes.text: Je to sploh kdo opazil? Kje pa, 'življenje gre naprej', nekaj, kar si velja vedno zapomniti!

nodes.source: 24th February 2006 - Friday
nodes.text: 24. februarja 2006 - petek

nodes.source: My first official blood test since my landmark one year clear date. Today's test will eventually confirm 'officially' if I am to make the one year of untraceable HCG markers in my blood. The chances of my Testicular Cancer coming back are diminishing as time goes by and passing the one year mark just makes it all look that much better!
nodes.text: Moj prvi uradni krvni test po prelomnem datumu enega leta brez raka. Današnji test bo nazadnje 'uradno' potrdil, ali bom dosegel eno leto brez zaznavnih označevalcev HCG v krvi. Možnosti, da se moj rak mod vrne, se s časom zmanjšujejo, in ko prečkaš enoletno mejo, je vse videti še toliko bolje!

nodes.source: Arrived at Hospital in a rush today. Got a lot of things going on in my life outside of hospital now, it's a comfort to come in and get checked up but sometimes feels like a chore. However, I wouldn't miss it for the world and my appointments can be made somewhat flexible if required. So despite the drag of driving to Charing Cross Hospital, it comes pretty high up on my agenda!
nodes.text: Danes sem v bolnišnico prispel v naglici. Zdaj se mi v življenju zunaj bolnišnice dogaja veliko stvari. Pomirjujoče je priti na pregled, a včasih se zdi kot nadležna obveznost. Kljub temu ga ne bi zamudil za nič na svetu in po potrebi lahko termine nekoliko prilagodijo. Torej je kljub neprijetni vožnji do bolnišnice Charing Cross to precej visoko na mojem seznamu prednostnih nalog!

nodes.source: As soon as I walked through the door I was greeted by my friendly Phlebotomists. Another landmark today, I WATCHED for the first time, every detail, a big deal for me, but I was feeling strong so I went for it. The needle went in and I hardly felt a thing, 4 test tubes of blood taken (it amazes me how fast it spurts out!). One and most importantly for my tumour markers (HCG), two to monitor my general health (U&E's & FBC) and finally one for my testosterone levels.
nodes.text: Takoj ko sem stopil skozi vrata, so me pozdravili moji prijazni ljudje za odvzem krvi. Danes še en mejnik: prvič sem GLEDAL, prav vsako podrobnost. Zame velika stvar, a počutil sem se močnega, zato sem poskusil. Igla je šla noter in skoraj ničesar nisem čutil, vzeli so mi 4 epruvete krvi (osupne me, kako hitro brizgne ven!). Eno, najpomembnejšo, za tumorske označevalce (HCG), dve za spremljanje splošnega zdravja (U&E in FBC) in zadnjo za raven testosterona.

nodes.source: Spoke with Dr. Savage who also seemed happy the year had so far been clear for me! I showed him some amazing new images I have had created from an old CT scan, you can see them in the 'Results' section of my site, of which he was suitably impressed (thanks go to Antoine Rosset of OsiriX fame) and the Apple Mac of course!
nodes.text: Govoril sem z dr. Savageem, ki je bil tudi videti vesel, da je moje leto doslej minilo brez raka! Pokazal sem mu nekaj izjemnih novih slik, ki so mi jih ustvarili iz starega CT-posnetka. Ogledate si jih lahko v razdelku 'Rezultati' mojega spletnega mesta. Bil je primerno navdušen (zahvala gre Antoinu Rossetu, znanemu po OsiriXu) in seveda računalniku Apple Mac!

nodes.source: Got the all important physical examination out of the way, collected my X-Ray appointment form, arranged my next appointment and I was off.
nodes.text: Opravil sem nadvse pomemben telesni pregled, prevzel napotnico za rentgen, se dogovoril za naslednji pregled in odšel.

nodes.source: Once at the X-Ray department, I had to wait a little while for it to be taken. My name was called and it was all done in seconds, had a quick peek and all looked good to me. I collected quite a crowd of radiographers around me as I showed off the CT imagery and as with every time I visit them and tell my story they are amazed and pleased at my progress from what they can see was quite a nasty spread.
nodes.text: Na rentgenskem oddelku sem moral malo počakati na slikanje. Poklicali so moje ime in vse je bilo opravljeno v nekaj sekundah. Na hitro sem pokukal in vse se mi je zdelo v redu. Okoli mene se je zbrala kar skupina radioloških inženirjev, ko sem razkazoval CT-slike. Tako kot vsakič, ko jih obiščem in povem svojo zgodbo, so bili presenečeni in veseli mojega napredka po tem, za kar lahko vidijo, da je bila precej huda razširitev bolezni.

nodes.source: That was my last monthly check-up. I now move to every two months with chest X-Rays on alternate visits as before, obviously more spread out. A radiation break for my chest!
nodes.text: To je bil moj zadnji mesečni pregled. Zdaj prehajam na preglede na dva meseca, z rentgenskim slikanjem prsnega koša ob vsakem drugem obisku kot doslej, seveda v večjih presledkih. Odmor od sevanja za moj prsni koš!

nodes.source: I do hope this website is helping someone out there. Please feel free to email me to ask questions... don't be afraid.
nodes.text: Res upam, da to spletno mesto komu pomaga. Brez zadržkov mi pišite po e-pošti in postavljajte vprašanja... naj vas ne bo strah.

nodes.source: Unless anything changes, see you back here on April the 14th 2006, one year on from that scary operation (there will be new scar pictures)!
nodes.text: Če se kaj ne spremeni, se spet vidimo tukaj 14. aprila 2006, eno leto po tisti strašljivi operaciji (na voljo bodo nove fotografije brazgotin)!

nodes.source: April 2006 14th April 2006 - Friday
nodes.text: April 2006 14. april 2006 - petek

nodes.source: One year on, since that daunting day.
nodes.text: Eno leto po tistem zastrašujočem dnevu.

nodes.source: I remember it well, in retrospect I was totally distraught with worry, fear and anxiety. I could have filled buckets with the tears I shed. An operation that I was certainly not looking forward to.
nodes.text: Dobro se ga spomnim. Ko pogledam nazaj, sem bil povsem iz sebe od skrbi, strahu in tesnobe. S solzami, ki sem jih pretočil, bi lahko napolnil vedra. Operacija, ki se je zagotovo nisem veselil.

nodes.source: I went through a lot, although at the time it's happening to you it seems that you just have to get on with things and take each day as it comes. Dealing with the unknown seems easier in comparison. Looking back at the whole thing, it was massive and I'm very lucky to be here writing this!
nodes.text: Veliko sem prestal, čeprav se ti takrat, ko se ti to dogaja, zdi, da moraš preprosto nadaljevati in jemati vsak dan sproti. Spopadanje z neznanim se v primerjavi s tem zdi lažje. Ko zdaj gledam na vse skupaj, je bilo ogromno in imam veliko srečo, da sem tukaj in to pišem!

nodes.source: Having friends and family around me, supporting me was a blessing. Reading through the 14th April 2005's diary entry really touches me. It took a fair chunk out of my life to overcome the Cancer, which the effects of, particularly financial, are still with me. My body has been through a lot, only time will tell if I am to get rid of some of the lasting symptoms... the scars will be with me forever.
nodes.text: Blagoslov je bil, da sem imel okoli sebe prijatelje in družino, ki so me podpirali. Branje dnevniškega zapisa z dne 14. aprila 2005 se me res dotakne. Premagovanje raka mi je vzelo pošten kos življenja in posledice, predvsem finančne, so še vedno z menoj.
